events.feedback:
This one has **excellent raw material**, but it is also more prone to overstatement than the Silver Date Palm. The central story is very strong: **a native Florida palm that is essentially trunkless, heavily armed, extremely cold-hardy, pollinated by weevils, and whose foul-smelling fruits are eaten by bears.** That is plenty.

The main problem is that several claims have been pushed one step beyond what the evidence supports. I would rather have this page be a little less sensational and completely bulletproof.

## 1. Fix the cold-hardiness claim — **highest priority**

> "This is the most cold-hardy palm on Earth."

I would **cut this wording**.

The Needle Palm is certainly extraordinarily cold-hardy, and reputable Florida material says it can survive well north of its native range, including USDA Zone 6. ([FDACS][1])

But "most cold-hardy palm on Earth" is a superlative that needs a very strong comparative source. The attached record gives the even more specific claim:
